newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals futures end firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals futures end firmer.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended firmer across the board, supported by the yen's slip against the dollar and firmer spot metal prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from unchanged to four yen per gram higher. Benchmark August ended up four at 1,348 after hitting its life-of-contract high during the day.

Private investors were aggressively liquidating their longs and taking profits, taking advantage of a price rebound, while trade houses bought futures while selling spot gold in arbitrage trade, they said.
Bullion was quoted at $379.90/380.10 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $379.75/380.25 in New York on Wednesday.
Traders expected open interest of yen-based gold futures to fall further, reflecting heavy long-liquidation by private investors on Thursday.
They added private investors were likely to be sidelined after liquidating their positions as the market lacked momentum for any fresh buying.
One dealer at a foreign bank said spot gold was expected to move within tight ranges between $378 and $381 per ounce until the release of U.S. job data on Friday.
Silver futures ranged from 0.3 yen to 3.2 yen per 10 grams higher, with benchmark August finishing up 0.9 yen at 178.6 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from one yen per gram lower to four firmer. Benchmark August was up two at 1,368 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from four to eight yen per gram higher, with benchmark August finishing up eight at 435 yen.
Traders said Japan's physical palladium market continued to face an oversupply trend, reflecting sluggish demand from the electronic and automobile sectors.
